One card. One risk. One comeback.

A simpler version made after playtest feedback. ONE pile. ONE optional extra card. No rotated arrows, no three-card chains, no separate attack-confirmation step.

Rules & examples
Full rules, including when you can't play
  • Deal 4 cards to each player. Leave one face-up card in the middle, and the rest in the draw pile. When your turn ends, refill to 4 if any stock remains.
  • The arrow on the previous top card controls the next card: ↑ means equal or higher, ↓ means equal or lower.
  • Matching the previous number removes the entire pile from the game and ends your turn.
  • Otherwise, after playing your first card, you can finish your turn, or add exactly one legal card of a different number. The extra card is shifted to the right to make it visible.
  • On their turn, the next player can play any card matching your extra card's number to bounce the entire pile back to you. Their matching card is discarded and their turn ends. Or they may ignore the attack and play normally.
  • If you have no legal card and cannot bounce, trade any card in your hand for the pile's top card; your surrendered card leaves the game. Once the draw pile is empty, the first player with no cards wins. A final extra card must survive the next player's opportunity to bounce.

Design experiment, not a final game. This version deliberately replaces the confusing Chain flow and retires Twin Piles from the primary playtest. The old experiments remain available only as archives.
